`abstract class Backend`<br/>
**Known subtypes:** [`Lwjgl2Backend`](/reference/lwjgl2/lwjgl2backend/), [`Lwjgl3Backend`](/reference/lwjgl3/lwjgl3backend/), [`VulkanBackend`](/reference/vulkan/vulkanbackend/)<br/>
**Package:** `dev.joid.lib.bridge.backend` · **Module:** `core` · **Source:** [Backend.java](https://github.com/Zeldown/JOID/blob/main/core/src/main/java/dev/joid/lib/bridge/backend/Backend.java)

The base class of every backend, which connects JOID to a window, a graphics API and an audio device in one `register()` call.

## Description

An application never extends `Backend`: it creates the backend of its library, sets its options, calls `register()` once the window and its graphics context exist, then `frame()` once per iteration of its loop.

```java file="com/example/reference/backends/BackendLoop.java" region="loop"
```

A backend author extends it and implements the `create...` hooks, which `register()` calls in a fixed order.

## Method details

<a id="Backend-method-register"></a>

### register

`this register()` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>

**Throws:**

- `IllegalStateException`: … is already registered, call register() only once

Connects the backend to JOID, loads JOID and runs the [`JOID.onReady`](/reference/ui/joid/#JOID-method-onReady) callbacks: [What register() does](/use/learn/running/backends/#what-register-does) lists every step.
Call it once, on the thread of your loop, with the graphics context current; a second call throws an `IllegalStateException`.

<a id="Backend-method-frame"></a>

### frame

`this frame()` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>

Runs one frame of every UI bridge through [`UIBridgeRegistry.frame`](/reference/backends/uibridgeregistry/#UIBridgeRegistry-method-frame): resize when the window changed, update, clear and draw.
Call it once per iteration of your loop, between polling the events and showing the image.

<a id="Backend-method-getVersion"></a>

### getVersion

`String getVersion()` 

Returns the version of JOID that the backend was built for, read from `backend.properties`.

<a id="Backend-method-isRegistered"></a>

### isRegistered

`boolean isRegistered()` 

If `true`, `register()` has run.

<a id="Backend-method-createWindowBridge"></a>

### createWindowBridge

`IWindowBridge createWindowBridge()` <span class="joid-qualifier">hook</span> <span class="joid-qualifier">abstract</span> <span class="joid-qualifier">protected</span>

JOID calls it during `register()`, after the audio bridge, and registers the result in `BridgeHandler.WINDOW`.
Return the window bridge of your backend.

<a id="Backend-method-createRenderBridge"></a>

### createRenderBridge

`IRenderBridge createRenderBridge()` <span class="joid-qualifier">hook</span> <span class="joid-qualifier">abstract</span> <span class="joid-qualifier">protected</span>

JOID calls it during `register()`, after the window bridge, with the graphics context current, and registers the result in `BridgeHandler.RENDER`.
Return the render bridge of your backend.

<a id="Backend-method-createAudioBridge"></a>

### createAudioBridge

`IAudioBridge createAudioBridge()` <span class="joid-qualifier">hook</span> <span class="joid-qualifier">protected</span>

JOID calls it first during `register()`, unless `audio(false)` was set.
Return the audio bridge, or `null` to register none; it returns `null` by default.

<a id="Backend-method-createThreadBridge"></a>

### createThreadBridge

`IThreadBridge createThreadBridge()` <span class="joid-qualifier">hook</span> <span class="joid-qualifier">protected</span>

JOID calls it during `register()`, after the render bridge.
Return the bridge of your render thread, or `null` to keep the [`DirectThreadBridge`](/reference/bridges/directthreadbridge/); it returns a [`FrameThreadBridge`](/reference/bridges/framethreadbridge/) tied to the calling thread by default.

<a id="Backend-method-registerDefaults"></a>

### registerDefaults

`void registerDefaults()` <span class="joid-qualifier">hook</span> <span class="joid-qualifier">protected</span>

JOID calls it during `register()`, after the bridges.
It registers a [`WindowUIBridge`](/reference/backends/windowuibridge/) with `registerDefault` by default; override it to add what your backend needs in other registries, and call `super.registerDefaults()` to keep the default UI bridge.

<a id="Backend-method-attachInput"></a>

### attachInput

`void attachInput()` <span class="joid-qualifier">hook</span> <span class="joid-qualifier">protected</span>

JOID calls it during `register()`, after `registerDefaults()`, to connect the input of the window to `BridgeHandler.UI`; it does nothing by default.
A backend whose input belongs to the loop of the application leaves it empty and gives the application a forwarder to poll.
